state_ownership_review: One finger belongs only to a press received while this specific popup is visible. Unpaired opening release and unmatched drag are handled without root mouse forwarding.
Other finger or repeated press cannot steal the sole native mouse gesture. Matching release clears ownership before signal/mouse forwarding, avoiding hide callback/reentrant stale state.
Visibility changes and adapter exit clear ownership; hide/reopen/cancel cannot carry old release into a new popup lifecycle.
Any canceled touch retains original cancel-and-hide semantics, including foreign-finger cancellation. DOM cancel entry retains same policy and now clears ownership first.

Regular mouse input remains outside this adapter touch branch. Existing mouse-button/motion payload, coordinates and forwarding mechanism remain unchanged. No gameplay/audio/resource/RNG/global-emulation change.

covers: ordinary native mouse selection after orphan release
test_scope.remaining: Original registered underworld-ui and studio-input full native wrappers, actual Web DOM/touch and browser consumers remain to be run by root; bounded probe is not that acceptance.

classification: Independent pre-existing UI gesture-lifecycle defect correction, not behavior-preserving architecture refactor. Production379 architecture CI remains separately attributed.
lease: Reviewer ran no engine/browser and holds no main-write or engine lease. Root may apply exact two files and execute original checks immediately.
limits: No blanket first-release swallowing: a real visible popup press pairs its own release, and tests prove subsequent real taps work.
No claim that callback-native test reproduces real DOM touchcancel dispatch; browser verification remains required.
